body: matching white stripes cross the candle and clipboard. a name-sized patch on the candle has been scrubbed bare.
title: Candle beside the spare mark
gloss: A response bundle preserves a missing count, changed route, or erased identity.
rival_reading: A farm-program crew could have counted routes, repacked tools, or removed ownership marks during hurried field work; the objects do not prove a concealed public response.

body:
Photograph back: the cross marks the store used by the crop trial. One sample crate was removed before the inventory and left a blue outline on the floor.

I saved it from the bag of rubbish because there was a name on the reverse. The name was not on the list they posted.

It could be a mistake in the copying. The things stacked beside the page were real enough, and still waiting to be moved.
title: Cross beside the trial store
rival_reading: A disaster-response worker could have made the same observation; this personal paper does not identify who directed the work.

body:
Torn page: there should be sampling jars and boot covers here. The crop crew left them when two workers developed rashes and the planned collection was cancelled.

The first person who saw it called it routine. The second asked me to stop using the well until another visit could be arranged.

It could be a mistake in the copying. The things stacked beside the page were real enough, and still waiting to be moved.

body:
Personal farm log: “too big to secure” was the old packing floor. The trial team used only one bay, yet fresh powder reached the locked bays overnight.

We tried to finish the ordinary work around it. The notice changed faster than the deliveries, and no one came to collect what was left.

It could be a mistake in the copying. The things stacked beside the page were real enough, and still waiting to be moved.

body:
Receipt margin: count the sealed seed sacks again at the cross. The driver signed for twelve, while only eleven appear on the field tally.

Nobody agreed on whose list this belonged to. I left it where the next person would look for the things we still owed each other.

I could have mistaken the order in which those things happened. I could not mistake the empty place left for the person we had been waiting for.

body:
On a faded photograph: the handwritten name by the cross belonged to the man counting treated rows. His tally ends one row before the plants turned black.

I meant to ask about it in the morning. By then the person who could answer had gone with the last vehicle, and this was all that remained.

I could have mistaken the order in which those things happened. I could not mistake the empty place left for the person we had been waiting for.
